title: Inverse refinement mates give coherent common-refinement comparisons
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of schemes admitting a compactification, and let $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ have the objects $c=(j_c:X\hookrightarrow W_c,p_c:W_c\to Y)$ and proper refinements of [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Suppose this category is cofiltered: any two objects have a common refinement, and any two parallel arrows $a,b:d\to c$ admit $e:d'\to d$ with $ae=be$. All categories, functors, and natural transformations below are taken in a fixed universe [def-nagata-category, def-weil-size-convention].

Assign a category $\mathcal D_W$ to each scheme involved. For each proper $u:W\to V$ supply $R_u:\mathcal D_W\to\mathcal D_V$, with natural unital associative compositors $c_{v,u}:R_{vu}\cong R_vR_u$; in particular
$$R_w(c_{v,u})c_{w,vu}=(c_{w,v}R_u)c_{wv,u}.$$
For each compactification supply $J_c:\mathcal D_X\to\mathcal D_{W_c}$, and for every refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$ a natural transformation $\gamma_u:J_{c_2}\to R_uJ_{c_1}$. Assume the identity normalization $\gamma_1=1$ and the vertical-pasting equation
$$c_{v,u,J_{c_1}}\gamma_{vu}=R_v(\gamma_u)\gamma_v:J_{c_3}\longrightarrow R_vR_uJ_{c_1}.$$
Let $\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal D_X$ be a full subcategory on which each $\gamma_u$ is pointwise invertible. No invertibility is assumed outside $\mathcal E$, and no proper/open comparison for non-refinement squares is assumed. Put $F_c=R_{p_c}J_c$ and, on $\mathcal E$, define
$$\theta_u=R_{p_2}(\gamma_u^{-1})c_{p_2,u,J_{c_1}}:F_{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c_2}.$$
Then $\theta_1=1$ and $\theta_{vu}=\theta_v\theta_u$ as natural transformations on $\mathcal E$. More explicitly, with $p_2=p_3v$, both sides equal
$$R_{p_3}(\gamma_v^{-1})\,R_{p_3}R_v(\gamma_u^{-1})\,c_{p_3,v,R_uJ_{c_1}}\,c_{p_2,u,J_{c_1}}.$$
Parallel refinements $a,b:d\to c$ induce equal transformations $\theta_a=\theta_b$. For every common refinement $a:d\to c_1$, $b:d\to c_2$, the natural isomorphism $C_{12}=\theta_b\theta_a^{-1}:F_{c_1}|_{\mathcal E}\cong F_{c_2}|_{\mathcal E}$ is independent of $d,a,b$. For three compactifications these comparisons satisfy $C_{23}C_{12}=C_{13}$ and $C_{11}=1$. The conclusions are equations in the supplied categories; no evaluation functors or detection of equality by them are involved.

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), with flat.tex Tag 0ATU (lemma-compactifications-cofiltered); agent abstract inverse-compositor and parallel-arrow cancellation argument.

proof.text: Work throughout on $\mathcal E$. Write products of arrows in functional order. For a morphism $h:M\to N$ in $\mathcal E$, naturality of $\gamma_u$ says $R_uJ_1(h)\gamma_{u,M}=\gamma_{u,N}J_2(h)$. Multiplication by the two component inverses gives $J_2(h)\gamma_{u,M}^{-1}=\gamma_{u,N}^{-1}R_uJ_1(h)$, so the pointwise inverses form a natural transformation on precisely $\mathcal E$. Any functor $R$ carries inverse arrows to inverse arrows: $R(t)R(t^{-1})=R(1)=1$ and similarly in the reverse order. Hence each displayed $\theta_u$ is a natural isomorphism, with inverse $c_{p_2,u,J_1}^{-1}R_{p_2}(\gamma_u)$. For identity refinements, substitute $\gamma_1=1$ and the supplied unital compositor normalization to get $\theta_1=1$. All reassociation below uses the category identity and associativity laws of [def-nagata-category].

source.place: Agent expansion of the supplied inverse comparisons; Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), formal identity normalization.

proof.text: Fix $u:c_1\to c_2$, $v:c_2\to c_3$ and $M\in\mathcal E$. Temporarily put $A=J_1M$, $B=J_2M$, $D=J_3M$, $U=\gamma_{u,M}:B\to R_uA$, $V=\gamma_{v,M}:D\to R_vB$, $W=\gamma_{vu,M}:D\to R_{vu}A$, and $C=c_{v,u,A}$. The assumed pasting equation is $CW=R_v(U)V$. Multiplying by the inverses shows $W^{-1}=V^{-1}R_v(U^{-1})C$: composing the proposed inverse with $W$ gives $V^{-1}R_v(U^{-1})R_v(U)V=1$, and composing in the other order gives $W W^{-1}=1$ by the same equation. Thus no inverse outside $\mathcal E$ is used.

source.place: Agent inverse algebra applied to the assumed vertical-pasting equation; Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose) is the geometric motivation.

proof.text: Apply $R_{p_3}$ to the inverse formula in Step 2 and substitute it in the definition of $\theta_{vu,M}$. This gives $R_{p_3}(V^{-1})R_{p_3}R_v(U^{-1})R_{p_3}(C)c_{p_3,vu,A}$. The assumed compositor associativity, with $(w,v,u)=(p_3,v,u)$, is $R_{p_3}(C)c_{p_3,vu,A}=c_{p_3,v,R_uA}c_{p_3v,u,A}$. Since $p_3v=p_2$, substitution gives exactly the explicit four-factor expression in the statement.

source.place: Agent substitution of the supplied compositor equation; Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), composition identifications.

proof.text: Expanding the other composite gives $\theta_{v,M}\theta_{u,M}=R_{p_3}(V^{-1})c_{p_3,v,B}R_{p_2}(U^{-1})c_{p_2,u,A}$. Naturality of $c_{p_3,v}:R_{p_2}\to R_{p_3}R_v$ at $U^{-1}:R_uA\to B$ reads $c_{p_3,v,B}R_{p_2}(U^{-1})=R_{p_3}R_v(U^{-1})c_{p_3,v,R_uA}$. Substituting this identity yields the expression from Step 3. Therefore $\theta_{vu}=\theta_v\theta_u$; this is equality of natural transformations since their components at every $M\in\mathcal E$ agree.

source.place: Agent naturality calculation for inverse refinement comparisons; Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose).

proof.text: For parallel refinements $a,b:d\to c$, the explicitly assumed cofilteredness supplies $e:d'\to d$ with $ae=be$. Refinement composition is composition of the underlying proper maps, as in [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Step 4 gives $\theta_a\theta_e=\theta_{ae}=\theta_{be}=\theta_b\theta_e$. Right multiplication by $\theta_e^{-1}$ proves $\theta_a=\theta_b$. This does not assert that $a=b$, or that the refinement squares are cartesian.

source.place: Agent cancellation using the cofilteredness assumed in the item; compare flat.tex Tag 0ATU (lemma-compactifications-cofiltered), proof (a), equalizing parallel arrows.

proof.text: If $(a:d\to c_1,b:d\to c_2)$ is a common refinement and $t:e\to d$ is any further refinement, Step 4 and inverse cancellation give $\theta_{bt}\theta_{at}^{-1}=(\theta_b\theta_t)(\theta_a\theta_t)^{-1}=\theta_b\theta_t\theta_t^{-1}\theta_a^{-1}=\theta_b\theta_a^{-1}$. Thus further refinement leaves the span comparison unchanged, as an equation of natural transformations on $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Agent span cancellation; Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), proof, independence of choices via common refinements.

proof.text: Take two spans $(d,a,b)$ and $(d',a',b')$ between $c_1,c_2$. The assumed common-refinement property gives $r:e\to d$ and $s:e\to d'$. The arrows $ar,a's:e\to c_1$ are parallel, so Step 5 gives $\theta_{ar}=\theta_{a's}$; likewise $\theta_{br}=\theta_{b's}$. Step 6 now gives $\theta_b\theta_a^{-1}=\theta_{br}\theta_{ar}^{-1}=\theta_{b's}\theta_{a's}^{-1}=\theta_{b'}\theta_{a'}^{-1}$. This proves independence of all three choices $d,a,b$, including the case of different arrows from the same common-refinement object.

source.place: Agent common-refinement and parallel-arrow argument; Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), independence-of-choices paragraph, and flat.tex Tag 0ATU (lemma-compactifications-cofiltered), proof (a).

proof.text: For $c_1,c_2,c_3$, first choose $d\to c_1,c_2$, then choose a common refinement $e$ of $d$ and $c_3$. Composition gives arrows $t_i:e\to c_i$ for all three indices. By Step 7 all three comparisons can be computed on these spans. Consequently $C_{23}C_{12}=(\theta_{t_3}\theta_{t_2}^{-1})(\theta_{t_2}\theta_{t_1}^{-1})=\theta_{t_3}\theta_{t_1}^{-1}=C_{13}$. To compute $C_{11}$ choose the span $(c_1,1,1)$; Step 1 gives $C_{11}=1$. All inverses, compositions and cancellations took place in the supplied functor categories on $\mathcal E$; no evaluation or equality-detection hypothesis was introduced.

source.place: Agent cocycle cancellation completing the common-refinement argument of Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition).

lean.statement: theorem refinement_inverse_mate_comparisons [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsCofiltered (Compactification f)] : (∀ c : Compactification f, T.theta E hE (𝟙 c) = Iso.refl (T.restricted E c)) ∧ (∀ (c d e : Compactification f) (r : c ⟶ d) (s : d ⟶ e), (T.theta E hE (r ≫ s)).hom = (T.theta E hE r).hom ≫ (T.theta E hE s).hom ∧ ∀ M : E.FullSubcategory, (T.theta E hE (r ≫ s)).hom.app M = (T.comp r.hom d.g c.g r.hom_g).hom.app ((T.J c).obj M.obj) ≫ (T.comp s.hom e.g d.g s.hom_g).hom.app ((T.R r.hom).obj ((T.J c).obj M.obj)) ≫ (T.R e.g).map ((T.R s.hom).map ((T.restrictedGamma E hE r).inv.app M)) ≫ (T.R e.g).map ((T.restrictedGamma E hE s).inv.app M)) ∧ (∀ (c d : Compactification f) (a b : c ⟶ d), (T.theta E hE a).hom = (T.theta E hE b).hom) ∧ (∀ (c d a b : Compactification f) (r : a ⟶ c) (s : a ⟶ d) (r' : b ⟶ c) (s' : b ⟶ d), T.compare E hE r s = T.compare E hE r' s') ∧ (∀ (c₁ c₂ c₃ a b d : Compactification f) (r₁ : a ⟶ c₁) (r₂ : a ⟶ c₂) (s₂ : b ⟶ c₂) (s₃ : b ⟶ c₃) (t₁ : d ⟶ c₁) (t₃ : d ⟶ c₃), (T.compare E hE r₁ r₂).hom ≫ (T.compare E hE s₂ s₃).hom = (T.compare E hE t₁ t₃).hom) ∧ (∀ (c a : Compactification f) (r s : a ⟶ c), T.compare E hE r s = Iso.refl (T.restricted E c))
